newsitem.title: USA: American Brands to spin off Gallaher tobacco unit.
newsitem.headline: American Brands to spin off Gallaher tobacco unit.

text.p: American Brands Inc. said Tuesday that it was completing its exit from the tobacco business as the legal and regulatory climate for cigarette companies becomes ever more onerous in the United States.

Shares of American Brands shot up 10 percent after the company, which also sells liquor, sports equipment and household hardware products, said it will spin off its British-based Gallaher tobacco business and then change its own name to Fortune Brands.
American Brands stock rose $4.625, or 10.1 percent, to $49.125 on the New York Stock Exchange in early trading.

The company, whose products include Jim Beam bourbon, Master Locks and Titleist, Foot-Joy and Cobra golf equipment, said that as part of the divestiture, Gallaher will pay Fortune Brands about $1.4 billion.
After the deal goes through, the company said, the new Fortune Brands will use the after-tax proceeds of about $1.25 billion to pay down short-term debt.

American Brands, which sold off its U.S. tobacco operations in 1994, said the Gallaher spinoff will strengthen the British-based company by removing it from the current harsh environment for cigarette makers in the United States, while also removing the future Fortune Brands from the potential liabilities of the tobacco industry.

"Since Gallaher will be recognised more clearly as a U.K./European tobacco manufacturer operating in an environment significantly different from the current U.S. tobacco litigation and regulatory environment, the value inherent in that operation should be more apparent," the company said in announcing the break-up.

The move comes at a time when the business environment for tobacco sales in the United States has never been more threatening, with lawsuits mounting and a new level of regulatory oversight being undertaken by federal authorties.

With sales of over $6.5 billion for the 12 months through June, Gallaher, whose major brands include Benson and Hedges and Silk Cut, is the tobacco market leader in Britain, with strong international sales, principally in Europe.

American Brands, which will retain its headquarters in Old Greenwich, Conn., said the move will allow it to concentrate on its other business lines, which produced $4.6 billion in sales in the 12 months through June.

"The spinoff will allow the managements of the two companies to focus exclusively on strategies and objectives geared to the very different financial, investment and operating characteristics and growth potential of their companies," American Brands Chairman Thomas Hays said.

"We believe that by creating two financially strong, publicly traded companies, each of which will be solidly positioned for profitable growth, we will enhance the prospects for both operations and increase shareholder value."

American Brands said that when it becomes Fortune Brands, it expects earnings growth of between 13 and 15 percent a year. "That's substantially higher than the 10 percent goal we had established for American Brands," the company said.
Eleven of its brands had sales of more than $100 million last year, including Jim Beam and DeKuyper liquors, Titleist, Foot-Joy and Cobra golf equipment and Master Lock padlocks.

The company said that after the split-up, Fortune's dividend would be about 80 cents a year and Gallaher's would be about $1.20, or 77 pence, although future dividends will be determined by the boards of the respective companies.
American Brands said it expected shares of Gallaher to be listed on the London Stock Exchange and on the New York Stock Exchange in the form of American Depositary Receipts.
It added that Gallaher plans to borrow about $1.4 billion to pay for the transaction, in addition to working capital requirements.
American Brands said that once the spinoff is completed, the new Fortune Brands will consider repurchasing up to 10 million Fortune shares.
Hays said that Fortune Brands' resources will give it broad flexibility to enhance its operations through internal development and acquisitions as well as to repurchase shares.
The company said the spinoff is contingent upon favourable tax rulings, which are more complex due to the international aspects of the transaction.
